idiom_name: generator function (function*) as the unfold + for..of accumulator as the fold
implementation_notes: A generator function is syntax-level coalgebra: each yield produces one layer on demand while the function's local state is the seed, so nothing is materialized between the unfolding and the folding. Because Array.prototype.reduce only exists on arrays, the fused fold over an iterator is a for..of loop with an accumulator (or a small reduceIter helper) - Array.from(gen).reduce(...) would reintroduce exactly the intermediate structure the pattern removes. Materialize deliberately when the sequence is data: caching, re-iteration, length and random access all require an array, and generators are single-shot.
pitfalls: Generators are single-shot: a second for..of over the same generator object yields nothing, so expose a factory (function returning a fresh generator) instead of the object.
Array.prototype.reduce cannot consume an iterator; writing Array.from(gen).reduce(op, init) is the two-pass version and defeats the pattern.
yield* recursion over a deep structure still grows the call stack, and an unclosed generator keeps its frame alive until GC - generators do not make deep recursion stack-safe.
